key_insight: PRISM automates multi-phase CT subtraction imaging for RCC by combining isotropic interpolation, kidney segmentation, deformable registration, and color-coded enhancement maps to replace subjective visual phase comparison.
clinical_relevance: This could make renal tumor characterization more consistent and efficient by highlighting enhancement patterns that help distinguish lesions across CT phases.
method: Loaded DICOMs and classified contrast phases automatically
Used RIFE for isotropic interpolation and TotalSegmentator v2 for kidney segmentation
Applied rigid, affine, and B-spline registration with SimpleITK, then generated dual-channel subtraction visualizations
evidence_signal: In 200 registrations across five patients and five experiments, the authors found a 40 mm B-spline grid, 5% metric sampling, and a single-level pyramid gave near-optimal registration performance, with subtraction thresholds showing a tradeoff between signal-to-noise and retained enhancing volume.
watch_item: The pipeline’s performance and threshold choices were evaluated on a small patient set, so broader validation and robust integration into varied clinical workflows are still needed.
paper_title: PRISM: Phase-Resolved Isotropic Subtraction Mapping for Automated Multi-Phase CT Digital Subtraction Angiography
